 Judgment
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That, on 23.03.2023 at about 6-20 p.m. the petitioner was riding two wheeler bearing registration No.KA-05/JN-7360 along with pillion rider by name Asif,
proceeding on SH-9 road, Rajarappalu Gudisalu, Gowribidanur Taluk, when they reached near Dodda Kurugodu cross, at that time, driver of Bus bearing registration No.KA-51/B-7478 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering to human life came from opposite side i.e., Hindupura side and dashed the petitioner's vehicle.
As a result of which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government, Hospital, Gowribidanur, for first aid, then he was shifted to Life Care Unit C/o K.K.Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery and spent more than Rs.10,00,000/- towards medicines, attendant charges,
food and nourishment etc.
4.

It is further contended that prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and aged about 21 years, doing tailoring work and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month and he used to spend the said amount for the maintenance of his family members.
After the accident, he could not do any work due to accidental injuries.
5. It is contended that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the Bus bearing registration No.KA-51/B-7478.
In this regard, case was registered against driver of said vehicle by the jurisdictional Gowribidanur Rural Police in Crime No.53/2023.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition seeking compensation.

6. In response to issuance of notices, the respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal,
remained absent, hence he was placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.

7. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 admitted about the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Bus bearing registration No.KA-51/B-7478 and the liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

It is contention of the respondent No.2 that alleged accident occurred due Mujaheed Alias Mujahid vs Bettaswamy on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115392329/
2 to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner himself and not on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective D.L. and F.C. as on the date of accident, hence there is a clear violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the petition.
Ultimately stated that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner, is highly excessive, exorbitant and without any basis.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 23.03.2023 at about 6.20-6.30 p.m. on SH-9 Road, near Doddkurugodu cross, Rajarappalu Gudisalu, Gowribidanur Taluk,
Chikkaballapura due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus bearing registration No.KA-51-B-7478 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, at what rate and from whom?
3) What order or award?
9. In order to substantiate the case, the petitioner has placed his affidavit evidence in lieu of examination- in-chief, who examined as PW1 and got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P19.
Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of MRO of K.K. Hospital as PW2 and got marked Ex.P20 to Ex.P22.

In addition to his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.S.A.Somashekara as PW3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P23 & Ex.P24.
10.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 got examined Superintendent of R.T.O, Electronic city,
Bengaluru as RW1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.

Further examined its Legal Executive as RW2 and got marked documents as Ex.R3 and Ex.R4.
11.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.

12. My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3: As per final order,
 for the following:
 R E A S O N S  ISSUE No.1:-

3 13.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Bus bearing registrationNo.KA-51/B-7478 the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.

14. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, but seriously disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 remained as silent spectator in this case.

15. In the light of the rival contentions of both the parties, on going through the above issue burden is on the petitioner to prove the above issue on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
16. The petitioner in order to prove his case got examined himself as PW1.
He has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon the police documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.
Ex.P1-copy of F.I.R. Ex.P2-copy of the first information statement, Ex.P3- copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P4- copy of spot sketch, Ex.P5- copy of IMV report,
Ex.P6- true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P7-Notice u/s 133 of IMV Act, Ex.P8- reply to the notice u/s 133 of IMV Act and Ex.P9-copy of charge sheet.

17. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that based upon the first information statement given by one Mr.Alla Bakash, the S.H.O. of Gowribidanur Rural Police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 &
304(A) of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the Investigation Officer of the case has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279, 338, 304(A) of IPC and Section 192(A) of IMV Act.
18. Though the respondent No.2 has examined its Manager as RW2, but his evidence will not much helpful to disprove the case of the petitioner.

19. Apart from this, at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondent No.2 about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.

20. In the light of the evidence placed on record, it is crystal clear that, the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the Bus bearing registration No.KA-51/B-7478.
As such, the petitioner has placed satisfactory and convincing evidence on record to prove the above issue.
Hence, I am answering the issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2:
21.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injuries cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/

entities.text: Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation''.

Pain and Sufferings;
23.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P6.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1)Comminuted fracture right Humerus,
2) Right lower end of femur open fracture with crush injury 3) Right tibia and fibula compound open fracture 4) Right patella fracture,
24.
In connection with the above said injuries the doctor is of the opinion that the above said injuries are grievous in nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summary issued by Life Care Unit Hospital, at Ex.P10 reveals that petitioner was admitted from 23.03.2023 to 14.04.2023.
Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of MRO of KK Hospital as PW2.
He has placed authorisation letter, case sheet and x-ray at Ex.P20 to Ex.P23.
In addition to his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.S.A.Somashekar as PW3.

He has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained comminuted fracture of right humerus, right lower end of femur open with crush injury, right tibia and fibula compound fracture and right patella fracture.

Petitioner underwent surgery of ORIF right humerus with DCP, extensive wound debridement of right thigh, ORIF of right femur with tibia graft, ORIF right tibia with LCP and iliac bone graft all on 24.3.2023 and above knee amputation under GA on 11.4.2023.

He has placed clinical notes and x-ray at Ex.P23 &
Mujaheed Alias Mujahid vs Bettaswamy on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115392329/
5 Ex.P24.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
25.
PW1 has stated that, he was doing tailoring work and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
In order to prove the same the petitioner has not placed any documents.
In the absence of the documents, it is apt to be considered notional income of the petitioner.
On going through the discharge summary issued by Life Care Unit Hospital, at Ex.P10 reveals that petitioner was admitted from 23.03.2023 to 14.04.2023.

During the period of treatment, definitely,
there was some difficulty to his to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of six months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.96,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
26.
The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses produced medical bills at Ex.P13 to the extent of Rs.9,20,466/- along with receipts and precritions at Ex.P16 & Ex.P17.
Except the suggestion there are no contra materials available on record to disprove the medical bills.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,20,466/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
27.
As per the medical records the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries of right lower end of femur open fracture with crush injury and the above knee amputation under GA 11.4.2023.
On perusal of photographs at Ex.P14 clearly reflects that the above knee amputation was done.

As per the records, for his injuries, he took treatment in KK Hospital from 23.03.2023 to 14.04.2023,
definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
28.
The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P6 goes to show that, he had sustained grievous injuries for which he took the treatment as an inpatient.

To substantiate this, the petitioner had placed wound Mujaheed Alias Mujahid vs Bettaswamy on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115392329/
6 certificate for consideration.
Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.S.A.Somashekar examined as PW3.

PW3 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained comminuted fracture of Right humerus, Right lower end of femur open with crush injury, right tibia and fibula compound fracture and Right patella fracture.

Further the petitioner underwent surgery in the form of ORIF right humerus with DCP, extensive wound debridement of right thigh, ORIF of right femur with tibias graft, ORIF right tibia with LCP and isiac bone graft on 4-03-2023 and above knee amputation under G.A. On 11-04-2023.
29.

Further PW3 has stated that, at the time of examination of the petitioner, petitioner is mobilised on a wheel chair, right sided A/K amputee of mid third level surgical, x-ray shows right sided A/K amputee at mid third level, delayed union fracture distal humerus with implants in situ.

He has placed clinical notes and x-ray at Ex.P23 & Ex.P24.
30.
At the time of cross-examination of PW3, stated that he is not the treated doctor.
Further stated that, right humerus has been operated and right lower limb above knee is amputated.
PW3 has admitted that now humerus fracture is united.
It is difficult for the petitioner to carry out sitting work also.
Further denied the suggestion that he has assessed the disability of the petitioner on higher side.

31.Over all appreciation of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, as well as his age, as on the date of the accident, and the nature of the work he was doing as on the date of the accident, along with the appreciation of evidence of PW2 in toto
, I am of the view that, the PW3 has expressed the percentage of disability wholebody as 66%.
Due to the accident the petitioner had total amputation of the right lower limb at the junction of middle third.
As such, the disability is not only the physical disability, but also he will face life long functional disability towards his day-to-day life as well as towards his work for avocation.
Accordingly, it is apt to take the functional disability of the petitioner as 60%.
The same will meet the ends of justice.
32. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 21 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed Aadhar card and D.L marked at Ex,P11 & Ex.P12 for consideration.
On going through the said documents, the date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 01.01.2003.
The accident occurred on 23.03.2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 20 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '18' is to be taken into consideration.

33. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident he was doing tailoring work and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/-
per month.
There is no iota of documents to show the income of the petitioner.
In the absence of the material documents, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2023.
As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.16,000/- for the year 2023.

Since the petitioner had lost one leg, consequent upon Mujaheed Alias Mujahid vs Bettaswamy on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115392329/
7 the accident, 40% future prospects also to be considered herein.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the petitioner's income has been taken as Rs.16,000/- per month.
If, future prospects of 40% is taken into consideration, it will comes at Rs.6,400/-.
In toto, the income of the petitioner is at Rs.22,400/- per month.

34. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.22,400 X 12 X18 X 60/100 = Rs.29,03,040/-.
Loss of amenities;
35.

On going to the injuries mentioned in the wound certificate, and also as per the evidence of the doctor PW3, fully discussed above, it is pertinent to note that, due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner's right lower limb was amputated.
Since leg important organ in the human body, to lead normal life, loosing one leg, definitely will cause great hardship to the injured.
Due to the said disability, he will suffer not only physically, but also, psychological impact too will cause to him.
Though no fault on his side, he has to suffer a lot before the society, in his young age.
By looking in to the photos placed by the petitioner also, reveals the genuineness of the problem of the petitioner.
And he has to to lead his future life along with the said permanent disability.

By keeping in mind about the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident and its consequences and also by taking in to consideration of the age criteria and future of the petitioner, some liberal approach is needed, to consider the compensation of the petitioner, under this head.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of amenities.

Loss of Marriage prospects;
36.
As observed above, the right leg of the petitioner was amputed.
The said amputation of the leg in the accident not only taken away the avocation of petitioner it also taken away the enjoyment of life of the young age of the petitioner.
It is not possible to fill-up the same by awarding compensation.
The petitioner was aged about 21 years.

By looking in to the condition of the petitioner, after the accident, along with the medical documents and opinion expressed by the doctor, definetly, the petitioner will lose the marriage prospects, as desires by a common man.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of marriage prospects.

Future Medical Expenses;
37.
PW3 has deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs surgeries for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.40,000/- in private set up.
Further deposed that, the petitioner needs a Sophisticated A/K Prosthesis which is very expensive and runs in lakhs.
In the cross examination he has deposed that he has not given separate estimation for removal of implants.
He has suggested for artificial limb.

However, by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and Mujaheed Alias Mujahid vs Bettaswamy on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115392329/
8 escalation of rates in the medical field, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.2,00,000/-
under the head of future medical expenses.

38. In view of my due discussions held above, on various aspects, the petitioner is entitled for compensation in toto, under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 1,50,000-00  2.Loss of income during Rs. 96,000-00  laid-up period and rest  period  3.Medical expenses Rs. 9,20,466-00 4.Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 1,50,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income due Rs.29,03,040-00 to disability 6.
Loss of Amenities Rs. 1,00,000-00 7.
Marriage prospects Rs. 1,00,000-00 7.
Future Medication Rs. 2,00,000-00 Total Rs.46,19,506-00 39.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.46,19,506/- (Rupees forty six lakhs nineteen thousand five hundred and six only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

LIABILITY:
40.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Bus bearing registration No.KA-51/B-7478 alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
41. The respondent No.2 had contended that the offending vehicle had no valid permit as on the date of accident.
In order to substantiate its contention examined its Legal Executive as RW2.

He Mujaheed Alias Mujahid vs Bettaswamy on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115392329/
9 has deposed that at the time of accident, there was no route permit towards Gowribidanur to Hindupur road, SH-9, to the private bus bearing No.KA-51-B-7478 and had permit only to ply Bengaluru Urban District only and the owner by allowing such a vehicle to ply on the road has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

sentences.text: After thorough investigation the jurisdictional police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the bus under section 279, 337, 304(A) of IPC and Section 187, 192(A) of M.V. Act.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.

He has placed authorisation letter and policy as Ex.R3 & Ex.R4.
42.
Apart from this, the respondent No.2 also examined superintendent of RTO office, Electronic City as RW1.
She has placed authorisation letter and permit extract at Ex.R1 & Ex.R2.
She has stated that as per Ex.R2, from 3.1.2020 to 2.1.2025 the offending vehicle had valid permit only to Bengaluru District, there is no permit to ply on Gowribidanur-Hindupur road.
On perusal of Ex.R2 it is clear that the route area for which the permit is valid Bengaluru Urban District only.

Hence,
there is no permit to ply on Gowribidanur road.
43. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued that, the offending vehicle had no valid permit to ply on the Gowribidanur-Hindupur road.
Further the learned counsel has relied the judgment in case of Shri Venkatesh & Others passed in MFA No.967/2017 by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has confirmed the judgment and award passed by the tribunal fastening the liability on the owner of the offending vehicle who permitted to ply the beyond area permitted by the transport authority.

44. At this stage, it is relevant to rely the decision reported in 2018 ACJ 2430 between Rani and Others Vs. National Insurance Company Limited and others, Wherein it is held that, "in connection with the permit came to the conclusion to direct the insurance company to deposit the amount of compensation with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle."
45.

entities.text: 2018 ACJ 2430 between Rani and Others Vs. National Insurance Company Limited and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the light of the supra decision, I am of the view that, in the present case also there was no valid permit as on the date of the accident.
The same point has been clearly disclosed in the evidence of RW1 and the documentary evidence Ex.R2.

Though, there was no permit to fly on the Gowribidanur-Hindupur road, in view of existence of valid insurance policy at the time of accident,
the principle of pay and recovery has to be followed.
With due respect, the decision relied by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2, the principle laid down in the supra is not applicalbe to the present case on hand.

Further, I am of the opinion that, the principle laid down in case of Rani &
Others is aptly applicable to the present case on hand.

Accordingly, the respondent No.2, being the insurance company has to pay the compensation amount determined by this court with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization, with a liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle i.e., from the respondent No.1 through due process of law.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner u/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.46,19,506/- (Rupees forty six lakhs nineteen thousand five hundred and six only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondent No.2 being the insurance company has to pay the compensation amount determined by this court with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Thereafter, recover the same from the respondent No.1 being owner of the offending vehicle through due process of law.
Expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.

After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.500/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
As a result of which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
After the accident, he could not do any work due to accidental injuries.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition seeking compensation.
6. In response to issuance of notices, the respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal,
remained absent, hence he was placed exparte.
It is contention of the respondent No.2 that alleged accident occurred due Mujaheed Alias Mujahid vs Bettaswamy on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115392329/
2 to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner himself and not on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective D.L. and F.C. as on the date of accident, hence there is a clear violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
opennyai_summary.issue:
8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 23.03.2023 at about 6.20-6.30 p.m. on SH-9 Road, near Doddkurugodu cross, Rajarappalu Gudisalu, Gowribidanur Taluk,
Chikkaballapura due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus bearing registration No.KA-51-B-7478 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, at what rate and from whom?
3) What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Bus bearing registrationNo.KA-51/B-7478 the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.
Upon investigation, the Investigation Officer of the case has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279, 338, 304(A) of IPC and Section 192(A) of IMV Act.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,20,466/- towards medical expenses.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.
The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
Due to the accident the petitioner had total amputation of the right lower limb at the junction of middle third.
As such, the disability is not only the physical disability, but also he will face life long functional disability towards his day-to-day life as well as towards his work for avocation.
Accordingly, it is apt to take the functional disability of the petitioner as 60%.
There is no iota of documents to show the income of the petitioner.
In the absence of the material documents, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.16,000/- for the year 2023.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of amenities.
Loss of Marriage prospects;
36.
After thorough investigation the jurisdictional police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the bus under section 279, 337, 304(A) of IPC and Section 187, 192(A) of M.V. Act.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.
On perusal of Ex.R2 it is clear that the route area for which the permit is valid Bengaluru Urban District only.
Hence,
there is no permit to ply on Gowribidanur road.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has confirmed the judgment and award passed by the tribunal fastening the liability on the owner of the offending vehicle who permitted to ply the beyond area permitted by the transport authority.
In the light of the supra decision, I am of the view that, in the present case also there was no valid permit as on the date of the accident.
Though, there was no permit to fly on the Gowribidanur-Hindupur road, in view of existence of valid insurance policy at the time of accident,
the principle of pay and recovery has to be followed.
Accordingly, the respondent No.2, being the insurance company has to pay the compensation amount determined by this court with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization, with a liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle i.e., from the respondent No.1 through due process of law.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of marriage prospects.
Loss of Amenities Rs. 1,00,000-00 7.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.46,19,506/- (Rupees forty six lakhs nineteen thousand five hundred and six only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner u/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.46,19,506/- (Rupees forty six lakhs nineteen thousand five hundred and six only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondent No.2 being the insurance company has to pay the compensation amount determined by this court with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Thereafter, recover the same from the respondent No.1 being owner of the offending vehicle through due process of law.
Expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.500/-.
Draw award accordingly.
